poems.note: The 1887 headnote marks the elevation of Patriarch Clement Bahouth in 1855; it does not establish the precise composition date. This occasional poem is not classified as devotional merely because its subject is a patriarch.

The headnote calls this a letter to a friend. The final couplet continues onto p. 10. The scans give ذابت عليها بالصبابة مهجتي and في الحي حي ما برحت كميت, correcting the consulted Wikisource transcription's garbled half-line and omission.
The headnote introduces a poem of praise; the following two-couplet birth chronogram is separately headed and is not included. Both scans read أقلامه, correcting the consulted Wikisource أفلامه.
The headnote describes the arrival of Princess Tāj al-Shihābiyya in Beirut for treatment. Both printings separately head and close these two couplets; they are not a fragment of the following poem.
The headnote marks the return from travel of the American Eli Smith. The 1887 poem continues over the page and ends before the separately headed greeting to Princess Tāj.

The 1887 headnote addresses Princess Tāj al-Shihābiyya after her departure to al-Wādī. The 1887 closing couplet reads أو انتقلت عن الأحياء; the third printing instead reads أو انتقلت عن الأوطان. The 1887 reading is retained. The second couplet reads واد له الشوق, not the consulted Wikisource وأدله الشوق.

The headnote introduces a separate greeting after Princess Tāj returned to Beirut. Its second and final couplet continues onto p. 13; the two printings both distinguish it from the longer preceding greeting.
Both printings separately head this elegy for the previously mentioned American Eli Smith. The 1887 opening couplet is at the bottom of p. 13; the remaining fifteen end before the next headed poem.
The headnote addresses congratulations to the mother of Amir Bashir Ahmad al-Lamʿī on his appointment in Mount Lebanon. The 1887 print reads جليل شان where the consulted Wikisource has جلل شان.
